note: Original SpeakWE practice questions written in the style of IELTS Speaking. Not official IELTS material. Imported as draft; approve each item in the Django admin before use.

part1_topics.title: Hometown
questions: Where is your hometown?
What do you like most about living there?
Has your hometown changed much since you were a child?
Would you like to live there in the future?

part1_topics.title: Work or studies
questions: Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your work or studies?
Is there anything you find difficult about it?
What would you like to do in the next few years?

part1_topics.title: Food
questions: What kind of food do you usually eat at home?
Do you prefer eating at home or eating out?
Is there any food you disliked as a child but enjoy now?
How often do you cook for yourself?

part1_topics.title: Weekends
questions: What do you usually do at the weekend?
Do you prefer relaxing or keeping busy on weekends?
Who do you usually spend your weekends with?
Was there a weekend recently that you really enjoyed?

part1_topics.title: Music
questions: What kind of music do you listen to most?
When do you usually listen to music?
Did you learn to play any instrument when you were younger?
Has your taste in music changed over the years?

part1_topics.title: Mobile phones
questions: How often do you use your mobile phone?
What do you mostly use it for?
Could you go a whole day without your phone?
Do you think people use their phones too much?

part1_topics.title: Weather
questions: What is the weather usually like where you live?
Which season do you like most?
Does the weather ever change your plans?
Do you check the weather forecast often?

part1_topics.title: Reading
questions: Do you enjoy reading?
What kind of things do you like to read?
Do you prefer printed books or reading on a screen?
Did you read a lot when you were a child?

part1_topics.title: Transport
questions: How do you usually get around your city?
Is public transport good where you live?
Do you enjoy long journeys?
Would you like to learn to drive, or do you already drive?

part1_topics.title: Friends
questions: Do you have a lot of friends or a few close ones?
How do you usually keep in touch with your friends?
What do you like to do together?
Is it easy to make new friends as an adult?

cue_cards.title: Describe a time you helped someone.
cue_cards.closing: and explain how you felt about it.
rounding_off: Do you often help people around you?
Is it easy for you to ask others for help?
part3: Why do some people find it hard to ask for help?
Should children be taught to help others at school?
Do people help their neighbours less than they used to?
Who should help elderly people: families or the government?

cue_cards.title: Describe a place you would like to visit.
bullets: what you would like to do there
cue_cards.closing: and explain why you want to visit this place.
rounding_off: Do you usually plan your trips carefully?
Would you go there alone or with others?
part3: Why do people enjoy travelling to other countries?
How has tourism changed the places people visit?
Is it better to travel when you are young?
Will people travel more or less in the future?

cue_cards.title: Describe a skill you learned that is useful to you.
bullets: when and how you learned it
cue_cards.closing: and explain why it is useful to you.
rounding_off: Was it difficult to learn?
Would you like to teach this skill to someone else?
part3: Which skills are most important for young people today?
Is it better to learn skills from a teacher or by yourself?
Do schools teach enough practical skills?
How might technology change the skills people need?

cue_cards.title: Describe a book or film that made a strong impression on you.
bullets: when you read or watched it
cue_cards.closing: and explain why it made such an impression on you.
rounding_off: Would you recommend it to your friends?
Do you usually read reviews before watching a film?
part3: Why are stories important in every culture?
Do films influence how people behave?
Will people still read printed books in the future?
Should governments support their country's film industry?

cue_cards.title: Describe a time you were very busy.
cue_cards.closing: and explain how you felt during that time.
rounding_off: Do you often feel busy?
What do you do to relax after a busy day?
part3: Why do people today seem busier than in the past?
Is it possible to have a good work-life balance?
Should companies limit working hours?
How does stress affect people's health?

cue_cards.title: Describe a person who has influenced you.
cue_cards.closing: and explain how they have influenced you.
rounding_off: Do you still keep in touch with this person?
Would you like to be similar to them?
part3: Who do young people look up to these days?
Can famous people be good role models?
Do parents have more influence than friends?
How do role models change as people get older?

cue_cards.title: Describe a gift you gave to someone.
cue_cards.closing: and explain how the person reacted.
rounding_off: Do you enjoy choosing gifts?
Do you prefer giving or receiving gifts?
part3: Why do people give gifts?
Is it better to give money or a present?
Have celebrations become too commercial?
How do gift-giving customs differ between cultures?

cue_cards.title: Describe a time you used technology to solve a problem.
cue_cards.closing: and explain whether you would do the same again.
rounding_off: Do you consider yourself good with technology?
Do you help older people use technology?
part3: How has technology changed the way people communicate?
Do people depend too much on technology?
Should children learn to code at school?
What problems might new technology create in the future?

cue_cards.title: Describe a park or outdoor place you enjoy.
cue_cards.closing: and explain why you enjoy this place.
rounding_off: Do you prefer going there alone or with others?
Is it busy at the weekends?
part3: Why are green spaces important in cities?
Do young people spend enough time outdoors?
Who should pay for public parks?
How can cities become better places to live?

cue_cards.title: Describe a goal you hope to achieve.
bullets: what you are doing to achieve it
cue_cards.closing: and explain why this goal is important to you.
rounding_off: Do you usually write your goals down?
Have you achieved a goal recently?
part3: Is it important to have long-term goals?
Do people give up on their goals too easily?
Should parents set goals for their children?
Is success more about hard work or luck?
